routes.description: The Santos–Guarujá crossing itself: ~400 m across the mouth of Latin America's largest port, today moving 21,000+ vehicles and thousands of walk-on riders a day on the state balsa. A foiling shuttle overlay adds fast, silent, all-weather headway on the single busiest short water crossing in Brazil.

The regulated Santos Centro–Vicente de Carvalho lancha line (official route length 2,200 m, ~12 min today). A foiling shuttle halves the water time and smooths the port-channel chop; distance uses the DH-published route length rather than straight-line.

The historic catraia small-boat crossing of the port channel between the Santos waterfront and Vicente de Carvalho — an adopted water-commuting habit ready for a clean, quiet upgrade. Slight margin added for the mid-channel dogleg around berthed shipping.

The lifeline to Ilha Diana, the fishing-village island in the estuary served today by the public boat from the Centro terminal. Coastal-wrap margin added: the navigable path follows the winding port channel north, not the straight line.
Ponta da Praia to Praia do Góes — a boat-only Guarujá beach across the harbour mouth, reached today by small launches from Ponte Edgard Perdigão. Short, iconic, and impossible by road.
The existing small-boat link from Ponta da Praia to Santa Cruz dos Navegantes on the Guarujá shore (the OSM-mapped 'Santos–Praia do Góes e N.S. dos Navegantes' service), landing by Marina Dolfin.
The state balsa crossing of the Canal de Bertioga at the north end of Santo Amaro island — the second Guarujá crossing in the same DER-SP/Semil travessias system, now folded into the 2025 PPP.

Cruise-passenger transfer from the Giusfredo Santini (Concais) terminal straight across to the Guarujá balsa head — replacing the 45 km road loop for the ~1 million passengers who move through Santos each season. Margin for the port-channel path.

The premium cruise arrival: Concais terminal direct to Porto Marina Astúrias on the Guarujá shore, marina to marina, past the working port. Today this transfer is a taxi over 45 km of highway; on the water it is a few silent minutes. Channel-path margin included.
Cross-channel connector between the cruise terminal and Vicente de Carvalho — the same axis the 2031 road tunnel will serve for vehicles, available on the water today.
Ponta da Praia to Porto Marina Astúrias — a direct marina spur linking the Santos leisure waterfront to Guarujá's main marina without the balsa queue.
Ponta da Praia to Ilha das Palmas, the private club island in Santos Bay (Clube de Pesca de Santos, founded 1934) — a classic members-and-events shuttle, boat-only by definition.
Guarujá marina to Ilha das Palmas across the open bay — the leisure triangle's third side.
Cruise-day excursion spur: Concais terminal to the Ilha das Palmas club island in Santos Bay.
A Santos waterfront line along the port channel, linking Ponta da Praia to the Centro/Valongo terminal — stitching the two ends of the city's water system together. Margin for the channel's curve.
Express diagonal: Santos Centro direct to the Guarujá balsa head down the port channel, collapsing a bus-plus-balsa commute into one seated ride.
Club shuttle between the Iate Clube de Santos nautical base on the Guarujá bank and Ponta da Praia — the yacht-club community's home crossing.
Guarujá balsa head south to Porto Marina Astúrias along the Guarujá shore — the marina feeder for the crossing.
Marina Astúrias to boat-only Praia do Góes — a two-minute beach hop around the Santa Cruz dos Navegantes point; small wrap margin for the headland.

The Canal de Bertioga run: from Ponta da Praia up the port channel and east through the mangrove-lined canal behind Santo Amaro island to the Bertioga crossing. Generous coastal-wrap margin — the navigable path winds through the estuary and canal, far off the straight line.
Santa Cruz dos Navegantes to Praia do Góes — the short hop between the fishing community's marina and its boat-only beach neighbour.
